questions.stem: When the technician arrived, the printer ___ already been repaired.

fr.rule: Action antérieure à une autre au passé → had + participe.
why_wrong: A : Récit au passé : plus-que-parfait.
C : Futur antérieur : le contexte est passé.
D : « was » + « been » est impossible.

en.rule: Action before another past action → had + participle.
why_wrong: A: Past narrative: past perfect.
C: Future perfect: the context is past.
D: 'was' + 'been' is impossible.

questions.stem: As soon as the contract ___ signed, we will begin production.

why_wrong: A : Le sens est futur.
C : Forme impossible.
D : Pas de « will » après « as soon as ».
A: The meaning is future.
C: Impossible form.
D: No 'will' after 'as soon as'.

questions.stem: By the end of June, the team ___ the migration to the new system.

fr.rule: By + date future → will have + participe.
why_wrong: A : Présent : ne marque pas l'achèvement futur.
B : « By the end of » appelle un futur antérieur (achevé avant).
D : Prétérit : le sens est futur.
fr.example: By May, I will have finished.

en.rule: By + future date → will have + participle.
why_wrong: A: Present: does not show future completion.
B: 'By the end of' calls for a future perfect (finished before).
D: Simple past: the meaning is future.
en.example: By May, I will have finished.

questions.stem: Look at those dark clouds: it ___ rain.

why_wrong: A : « has » ne s'emploie pas avec « rain » ici.
B : Passé : le sens est futur.
D : « would » est un conditionnel, pas une prévision à partir d'un signe visible.
A: 'has' does not fit 'rain' here.
B: Past: the meaning is future.
D: 'would' is a conditional, not a prediction from a visible sign.

questions.stem: I'm sorry, the manager is busy; he ___ with the client until noon.

fr.rule: Action en cours dans le futur → will be + -ing.
why_wrong: A : Prétérit : le sens est futur.
C : Plus-que-parfait : le sens est futur.
D : Présent parfait : pas de durée future.
fr.example: At noon, I will be working.

en.rule: Action in progress in the future → will be + -ing.
why_wrong: A: Simple past: the meaning is future.
C: Past perfect: the meaning is future.
D: Present perfect: no future duration.
en.example: At noon, I will be working.

questions.stem: The auditors had left ___ we found the error.

why_wrong: A : « unless » = à moins que.
C : « until » ne convient pas ici.
D : Contresens : ils sont partis avant la découverte.
fr.example: She had left before he called.

why_wrong: A: 'unless' = if not.
C: 'until' does not fit here.
D: Wrong sense: they left before the discovery.
en.example: She had left before he called.

choices: If the shipment arrived on Monday, we will start on Tuesday.
If the shipment is arriving on Monday, we start on Tuesday.
If the shipment will arrive on Monday, we will start on Tuesday.
If the shipment arrives on Monday, we will start on Tuesday.

why_wrong: A : Concordance incorrecte (prétérit puis futur).
B : Formes de temps incohérentes pour une prévision.
C : Pas de « will » après « if ».
fr.example: If it rains, we will stay.

why_wrong: A: Incorrect sequence (past then future).
B: Inconsistent tense forms for a prediction.
C: No 'will' after 'if'.
en.example: If it rains, we will stay.

questions.stem: They ___ the report before the board meeting started.

why_wrong: A : « started » est au passé : plus-que-parfait.
B : Présent : le contexte est passé.
D : Futur : le contexte est passé.
A: 'started' is past: past perfect.
B: Present: the context is past.
D: Future: the context is past.
